name: Diamond Ticket (Rubeus /tgtdeleg)
description: Request a legitimate TGT and modify its PAC to add privileged group memberships. Evades Golden Ticket detection since the TGT has valid DC signatures.

steps.label: Get krbtgt AES256 key via DCSync

examples.label: Diamond ticket adding to Domain Admins (512)

recommended.note: Get krbtgt AES256 key via DCSync
Use the elevated TGT (SID history / extra SIDs) to escalate from child to parent domain

notes: Uses /tgtdeleg to get a real delegated TGT, then modifies the PAC. The DC's server signature is real - evades standard golden ticket detection.

defense.why_it_works: Diamond Tickets improve on Golden Tickets by legitimately requesting a real TGT from the KDC (as the target user using /tgtdeleg on their existing TGT), then decrypting and modifying the PAC in-memory to add extra SIDs (like Domain Admins) before re-signing with the krbtgt hash. This produces a ticket that looks legitimate to KDC validation - it has a real timestamp, real encryption, and a real TGT structure - but with forged group memberships.
defense.prerequisites: krbtgt NTLM hash or AES key (from DCSync). A valid low-privilege TGT (via /tgtdeleg from an existing session). Rubeus /diamond or /tgtdeleg with PAC modification. Domain SID.
defense.impact: T1558.001 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Golden Ticket. Bypasses Golden Ticket detection heuristics (real ticket timestamp, legitimate AS-REQ exists). Full domain admin access via the forged PAC group memberships. Harder to detect than standard Golden Tickets.
defense.detection:
MDI: 'Golden Ticket usage' heuristics may miss Diamond Tickets (more advanced detection needed). Event 4768 (AS-REQ) does exist for Diamond Tickets (unlike pure Golden Tickets). Anomaly: group memberships in the ticket's PAC don't match the account's actual AD group memberships - requires PAC validation to detect. Microsoft Sentinel Analytics: 'Suspected Diamond Ticket Usage'.
Anomalous Kerberos activity: forged or stolen tickets by correlating malformed fields in logon events, RC4-encrypted TGTs, or TGS requests without corresponding TGT requests; suspicious processes accessing LSASS memory for ticket extraction (DET0522/AN1443).
Suspicious access to SSSD secrets database and Kerberos key material indicating ticket theft or replay; correlate anomalous file access with unusual Kerberos service ticket requests (AN1444).
Forging or replaying Kerberos tickets: monitor Unified Logs for anomalous kinit/klist activity and unusual authentication sequences (AN1445).
defense.artifacts: MDI alert if diamond ticket PAC inconsistency detected | Event 4768 (real AS-REQ from legitimate user) | Subsequent 4769 with escalated group memberships | PAC group SIDs inconsistent with user's actual groups in AD
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4769
| where Ticket_Encryption_Type=0x17
| table _time, Computer, Account_Name, Service_Name, Client_Address

index=sysmon EventCode=1 (CommandLine="*diamond*" OR CommandLine="*/tgtdeleg*")
| table _time, Computer, User, CommandLine
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4769 and TicketEncryptionType == "0x17"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, ServiceName, IpAddress
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
// PAC group SIDs inconsistent with account's real AD groups indicate a diamond ticket
defense.prevention:
Double-rotate krbtgt (same as Golden Ticket - Diamond Ticket requires krbtgt hash). PAC validation enforcement. MDI deployment with latest signatures. Enforce tiering - even with DA group in PAC, privileged access should require logon from PAW (Authentication Policy Silo). Monitor group membership anomalies via SIEM.
Active Directory Configuration: Reset KRBTGT account password twice (invalidates all golden tickets); rotate every 180 days.
Audit: Scan for insecure Kerberos configurations.
Credential Access Protection: On Linux, use SELinux to protect Kerberos key material.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Enable AES Kerberos encryption instead of RC4.
Password Policies: Service accounts should have 25+ character passwords; use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA).
Privileged Account Management: Limit domain admin to DCs only; restrict service account privileges.
defense.evasion: Diamond Ticket already bypasses most Golden Ticket detections by using a real AS-REQ. Use /aes256 for krbtgt to further blend with normal AES Kerberos traffic. Limit forged group memberships to the minimum needed.
defense.misconfiguration: krbtgt password never rotated. PAC validation not enforced. MDI not deployed or not updated. No SIEM correlation of PAC group membership anomalies.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# krbtgt hash available (from DCSync or NTDS.dit):
# Attacker has: krbtgt NTLM hash 31d6cfe0d16ae931b73c59d7e0c089c0
# + valid TGT for user 'helpdesk1' (low-priv)
# → Rubeus /diamond /tgtdeleg modifies PAC → DA-equivalent access
# Unlike Golden Ticket, AS-REQ log entry EXISTS → detection harder
defense.secure_config:
# Same mitigation as Golden Ticket - requires krbtgt hash:
# Double-rotate krbtgt (Microsoft script):
.\New-KrbtgtKeys.ps1 -Mode EnableAES
# Wait 10+ hours, repeat

# PAC validation:
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -Name ValidateKdcPacSignature -Value 1

# Enforce Authentication Policy Silos for DA accounts:
# Even with DA PAC, restrict which computers DAs can authenticate from
New-ADAuthenticationPolicy -Name 'DA-Policy' -UserAllowedToAuthenticateFrom 'PAW-Computers-SG'

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Windows Security Event Log, Sysmon for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Check for credential dumping artifacts (LSASS access, SAM hive reads, Kerberos anomalies)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Forges a Diamond Ticket - request a real TGT and rewrite its PAC, so it carries valid DC signatures (evades golden-ticket detection):
  diamond                   modify a legitimately issued TGT
  /tgtdeleg                 obtain a real TGT for the current user without their password
  /ticketuser:<user> /ticketuserid:<rid>   the user and RID the modified ticket is for
  /groups:512              inject Domain Admins (RID 512) into the PAC
  /krbkey:<aes256_key>     the krbtgt AES256 key to re-sign the PAC
  /nowrap                   single-line output
Inject it (/ptt) and you are DA with a ticket that looks KDC-issued.
